item.description:

Complex matching remains a challenge in the ontology matching field. Existing approaches are constrained by strong assumptions on their input: instance-based and rule-mining systems require populated ontologies and reliable links between their instances, while systems built on pre-trained encoders operate at the schema level but target primarily simple correspondences. item.title: A Love Story in Patterns: Twenty years of ontology design patterns, continued with language models
item.description:
Valentina Presutti A
Twenty years ago, a group of Semantic Web researchers set out to do for ontologies what the Gang of Four did for software. This talk retraces that love story, from NeOn and eXtreme Design to WOP, through an analysis of 788 papers. Language models now generate and match patterns, solving what we could not, while the bottleneck moves to trust. I argue that patterns matter more than ever, as the unit linking models, people and knowledge graphs, and outline the challenges ahead.

item.title: Scientific Editor — AI Protocol (Agent Skill)
item.description:
Rigjita Baldanova
An Agent Skill for editing and pre-submission auditing of scientific manuscripts in Russian and English. It verifies claims against sources and sources against reality, runs four gates (sources, internal facts, provenance and conflicts of interest, falsifiability), scores the text on a venue-calibrated rubric and returns an editorial recommendation.
